However, 'possibly' is the word: W/o enough room in between to actually put something (e.g., a book) onto the shelve, it makes little sense to install them. And, as it looked to me, many started out over the head of the bed (as in the picture). This being the case: the first shelf has to be high enough over the head of the student sitting on a chair/desk - the remaining space up to the top, for all practical purpose, is just enough for the one shelf it comes with when delivered. question_text: Can these wool mats be washed
answer_text: Hello and thank you for your question. We use questions and comments from customers to improve our products, and we greatly appreciate your interest. As to washing you mat, you can rinse it in a sink or tub. Do not rough it up or agitate it and do not put it in a washing machine. You can use some mild detergent and rinse with cold water. Let it dry out thoroughly after. You can set it in a dry sunny room, preferably directly in the sun. Or hang it in up in a dry room/space. Also using a fan directed at it can help speed the drying. If it is a dry sunny day, take the mat outside and set it in the sun. Flip it over periodically to dry it from both sides. Do not leave it out over night as morning dew can/will re-wet it. To reduce any musty smell, try sprinkling the mat with baking soda once it has completely dried. Allow the baking soda to sit for 30 minutes (or as needed) then vacuum the baking soda from the mat with a small hand-held vacuum.

question_text: """The leather is described as a """"pu"""" leather,  so what does """"pu"""" stand for????"""
answer_text: Pu leather is also known as bicast leather or split leather. Pu leather is short for polyurethane leather because the coating on this leather is made with polyurethane. So, what is polyurethane vs leather and how is the polyurethane applied to leather? The polyurethane coating is embossed on top of vinyl leather to look more like real leather that has been aged. It does have a layer of real leather in it, but the layer of leather has been split (hence the name, split leather) so the layer of real leather is thinner than with genuine leather. It was originally made for the shoe industry, but it was then adapted into the furniture industry.    The benefits of pu leather are that, due to its split backing with a polyurethane coating, it is more economical that 100% genuine cow leather. It also has a smoother, even grain which makes it easier to clean.    The main disadvantage is that, due to the thinness of the leather and the polyurethane coating, the material does not hold up for as long as 100% genuine leather. It's prone to tears or the polyurethane coating from peeling away from the leather backing after a few years. It is also prone to color transfer onto clothing or other pieces of fabric.

answer_text: LiPo batteries require perfect care. They can only remain fully charged on the shelf for no more than 48 hours or damage will start to occur. When not in use each cell has to be stored at 3.8 volts and should not sit unused for more than 6 weeks. Even when proper care is exercised LiPo batteries are still potentially dangerous. They are not suitable for youth sport use. NiMH batteries actually respond well to being fully charged and left full on the shelf until the next use. They do not require full cycling like the NiCd batteries of the 90's so they stand up well to the short attention span of younger drivers and this also increases life span because NiMH batteries decay when cycled. question_text: How many tests can you take with this kit?
answer_text: """This is like asking, """"How long is a piece of string?"""" Be very careful of folks selling kits that tell you brand ABC will take X tests, because they can't really know the answer. Some of the reagents are used at a rate of 5 drops per test and will give about 110 tests, some reagents are used at a rate of 2 drops per test, and some are used at a rate of one scoop (.05g) and may give about 200 tests. The most important reagents are used for titration and the amount you use of them is solely dependent on your sample size and the chemical concentrations you wish to keep in your pool. For example, R-0871 is used for testing chlorine. For a 25ml sample size (which is recommended by the manufacturer) you will use 5 drops per test for EACH PPM of FC. A FC level of 1 PPM would be 110 tests. 3 PPM would be for 36 tests and 7 PPM would be for 15 tests. So, you see, without knowing how YOU manage YOUR pool, trying to predict reagent usage is a marketing gimmick based on unknowable quantities. Remember to deduct your tests for CC, as they will also use the chlorine reagents... and again, nobody can predict this, as they have no idea the condition of your pool. Predicting reagent usage for testing CH and TA have the same issues. Know, too, that Taylor reagent bottles dispense at a rate of 25 drops per ml, which is NOT a standard rate dropper tip for anything other than tiny bottles of .5 ounce or less (think eyedrops). IF the reagent you purchase is not in a factory-calibrated bottle, it is likely dispensing at a standard rate, which is 20% different than the proprietary Taylor standard and all bets are off on any prediction of reagent usage and/or testing accuracy.....     PS  This kit is NOT for pools, it is for spas.  If you want a kit for testing a pool, order the K-2006-C kit.  It has a larger more useful box that contains 2-ounce bottles, not .75 ounce bottles.  For titration tests, 2 ounces will allow you to take 2.7 times more tests than this kit.  Caveat Emptor."""

answer_text: It is ceramics and also stoneware.  Ceramics or pottery refers to a process of forming, firing or baking and glazing or decorating a mixture of clay and other materials, then re-firing it to harden the glaze. The three ceramics are earthenware, stoneware and porcelain.  Stoneware is made from a particular type of clay that is fired at high temperatures, generally between 2,012 and 2,372 degrees Fahrenheit. It was first produced in China, during the Shang Dynasty (circa 1,400 BC).  Stoneware, named after its dense, stone-like quality after firing, is tougher and more durable than earthenware. And unlike earthenware, stoneware is waterproof. Earthenware can be coated with a vitreous (glasslike) liquid and re-fired and made waterproof.  The qualities of stoneware traditionally made it useful for dishes used for food, for drinking vessels and for storage. Today it is often used for cookware, bakeware and serving dishes.    Earthenware is often referred to as a ceramic or ceramic ware. Stoneware can be distinguished from earthenware by several qualities. Stoneware feels dense for its size and is often uncoated, undecorated or unglazed on the bottom. Earthenware has a white, chalky look when fired, whereas stoneware has a darker, textured look.   https://www.leaf.tv/articles/ceramic-vs-stoneware-dishes/

You'd then select an appropriate adhesion tensile test (lap, peel) to reflect the tapes intended-use, your testing should determine at what point the adhesive bond begins to degrade.  You'll have to baseline the adhesive/substrate at an ambient temp/time to assure your readings validity.  Enjoy!  Gordon S.

question_text: Why is this iodine clear and have zero flavor
answer_text: Hi CJ,   Great question! :)  Put simply our Nascent Iodine is Potassium Iodide, dissolved in water.   Iodine is an essential micronutrient, a mineral which is necessary to health but not naturally synthesized by the body. Iodine is naturally occurring in the soil and in certain foods, like fish and seaweed, and added to others, like Iodine-fortified salt. Under standard conditions, iodine is a solid, black-grey with a violet lustre. In solution, Elemental Iodine is unstable, so it will bond with another element, typically potassium or sodium. Thus, most Iodine in dietary supplements is in the form of potassium iodide or sodium iodide. Potassium Iodide is made by mixing potassium hydroxide with iodine; Potassium Iodide is also used in the iodization of salt.  We do not add sweetener as we wish to keep the product free of any unnecessary ingredients.   Please let our Customer Care Team know if you have any further questions.   With care,   Cara

answer_text: """Short answer: These lights will work well for your microgreens.     For microgreens and most plants, the Kelvin number is less important than the PAR output. (PAR = Photosynthectically Active Radiation) I bought some of these lights to test them and I have tested the entire Barrina line of LED lights for PAR output including the shop lights. All them will work for you. I did not test for Kelvin output. The specific frequency output on which the Kelvin rating is based, is provided as a graph by the manufacturer on the product page. But if I had to guess I'd say the output was 5,000 Kelvin or lower; so it's a relatively warm colored light which might be good for your purposes. Some researchers have gotten very high microgreen yields using lights with a higher red to blue ratio. My family grows microgreens and other crops commercially and we use Barrina LED lights almost exclusively. These lights will work well for greening your microgreens, but we actually don't even bother with lights specifically marketed as grow lights for our microgreens because we found that nearly any lights are adequate for that purpose and others are less expensive. We use the cheapest Barrina general utility strip lights and they work great. The specific lights we are presently using for our microgreens is the following light which has a kelvin rating of 6,500 which is a bright, cool white that is higher in the blue range: https://amzn.to/2QDJ2HW  We use 4 or 6 of these about 10"""" above four 10x20 flats of microgreens on 48""""x18"""" wire shelves. I recently began removing the diffusers from these lights because doing so more than doubles the PAR output making them more useful for our vegetable and flower seedling starts, but be advised that doing so absolutely voids the warranty. I don't care about the warranty. I've been using these lights for more than a year with no problems whatsoever and they are cheaper than dirt to replace in any case. question_text: Will this work on a early 1920s Remington rand safe?
answer_text: It is quite likely that you can utilize this lock on your safe. Remington-Rand commonly utilized a Yale combination lock on their safes that has the same footprint as most modern combination locks of today. There was a common exception to this late in their manufacturing and design production. They contracted Yale to produce a unique combination lock for them that integrated both the combination lock and mechanism to operate the locking bolt system. This lock is easily identified by a large drop handle extending from the center of the dial. question_text: Are these dimmable?
answer_text: LED's are diodes that emit light when the forward diode voltage is exceeded at some DC voltage level.  For this LED it is about 2vdc.  When that voltage level is exceeded the diode is forward biased and will start to draw current and begin to light up.  As you increase the DC voltage the LED will get brighter, if you keep increasing the voltage the diode will draw more current, get brighter and brighter, and eventually burn out( stopping current from flowing) due to excessive power dissipation.  So all LED's are dimmable with increasing voltage and current.  This particular LED is rated to produce a given light level at 3-3.vdc @ 20ma, which is about 60mw of power.  Varying the DC voltage to the LED will vary the current and one will be able to go from no light to lighted and vice versa, ie. dim.  One can also use PWM control circuit to also control lighting and dimming of an LED.

Now you have extended your network to the transmitter outside your building. At the far end you mount the receiver outside your building, then run an ethernet cable into your building and plug it into the POE port on the power inserter, then run an ethernet cable to your PC or to a wireless Hub (not router). I like the NetGear Nighthawk router/hubs for this as they are pretty easy to set up on a network without them automatically becoming a second router.    You don't want two devices to be the routers because of potential slow downs, or IP conflicts, of data and you probably want the devices in the other building to use your existing router for things like IP cameras, shared printers, etc.    The devices have a set IP number that may not be the same range as your router's network. The Ultra Thin Antenna comes with it's own cable and is ready to install right out of the box. However, if the cable from your tv is RG6 coaxial cable then yes I would connect that to the Ultra Thin Antenna. This is what I did. RG6 is thicker and thus better insulated and shields against signal interference better. Most of the cable companies use RG6 coaxial for their installations so you probably have it if you were paying for cable tv. The Ultra Thin Antenna is the best that I have used, at one point it found 74 channels, and by using the RG6 cable I get almost zero interference. I hope this helps you. FYI Before you connect your new antenna run two channel scans with no antenna connected at all. This will clear all the stored channel data on your digital tv and leave your tv with a clean memory. Attach the new antenna and run several scans while you change antenna locations each time to find the most channels and best signal. For me the antenna works best in a different room, off the wall and on a table or even on the floor. Good luck

question_text: I need to time wash cylces so I don't miss the rinse.  Do all events count at once, or can I use it for each event independently?
answer_text: You can time up to 3 separate events.  Press button 1 and you will notice an arrow next to that button.  If you press start the timer will start counting upward from zero.  If you want to time a fixed period (say 70 minutes) press the 1 button, and after you see the tiny arrow next to it, press the hour button once and press the minute button until it counts up to 10.  Then, press the start button and the timer will start counting backwards from 1 hour 10 minutes.  When timer 1 reaches zero, the alarm will sound off for around a minute, unless you push button 1 again to shut it off.  To use the other two timers, do the same as above except you press button 2 or button 3 first and confirm the little arrow beside that button before you begin.  If you want to stop any of the 3 timers before it is finished, press the its corresponding button (1,2, or 3) make sure the arrow is on the right number, and press the stop button.  If you want to resume that timer from the point you stopped it, just press start again.  If you want to reset it to zero, press reset.  If a timer isn't doing what you want,  the likely reason is that you forgot to press button 1, 2 or, 3 first to select that timer you want to affect.

Our pH On-The-Go filters use Zeolite and a blend of mineral balls that remove contaminants by Adsorption!    Adsorption is the process in which atoms, ions or molecules from a substance (it could be gas, liquid or dissolved solid) adhere to a surface of the adsorbent, in this case, our mineral ball blend.    The contaminants removed ionically bond to the massive surface area of the minerals and remain there, never leaching back into the water due to the strength of the ionic bond.    Hope this helps! question_text: Is it weather proof
answer_text: By itself, absolutely not.  It is basically pigment granules suspended in an alcohol/water base.  If you mix it in with something like epoxy, it will be as weather proof as the epoxy.  But, by itself, it becomes a chalky dusty layer of color that will come off in your hands, and if you pour water on it, it will wash off easily, which for me was actually a good thing.  I bought a bunch of the stuff based on the results in the example pictures, but the example pictures are made using the 'Unicorn Spit' as the pigment, using other components to actually make it a shellac of sorts, which means that non-toxic goes out the window, and using it by itself is not only temporary, but looks like cheap finger paint that they give to pre-school kids.  If you're willing to go the extra step and mix it into all kinds of other stuff, I have no doubt you can get some pretty cool results.  But if you're looking for an 'as is' solution, keep looking.

question_text: """Will this only work with dell server or will it work with any pc? another answer says it will be compatible with """"any pcie server"""". why """"server?"""""""
answer_text: Your instinct is correct here; I've been bitten before by buying HP branded dual-port 10G cards refurbished out of retired server machines. The problem is with poorly implemented SMBus lines on the PCIe interface -- pins 5 and 6. Server motherboards, for whatever reason, seem to be more forgiving of this (or are wrongly implemented the same way). When I put those HP cards in a modern desktop, the machine freezes and freaks out with beeping at boot time, etc. You can work around this problem by covering those pins with electrical tape, but it still doesn't behave quite right.    That said, another answer here is from someone running *this* card in a Dell desktop with no issues, so I suspect Mellanox didn't screw these cards up in that way and you should be fine.

question_text: Do you need to charge this before you use it for the first time?
answer_text: My lamp is now a couple of years old, so I can't speak specifically to new ones, but the instructions that accompany my lamp don't say you have to charge it first. However, my experience with probably hundreds by now of rechargeable electronic devices is that they nearly always say to fully charge them before using them the first time. I generally follow that principle, so I'd say to go ahead and charge it fully (blue light comes on) first. On the other hand, I have sometimes used devices without charging them fully the first time, and so far I've not been able tell that it affected the performance or longevity of the devices. Best be safe however.    I'd also follow the advice in my lamp's instructions to try to avoid deeply discharging the lamp before recharging it. It's usually not good to overcharge devices, either. I had to replace the battery in mine after a year or more of heavy use, and I was guilty at times of letting it get pretty dim before I recharged it, and I know I overcharged it at times, too. I think it's good to get into the habit of trying to keep the battery between about 60%-90%. The charger that came with my lamp seemed to be slow and erratic to me, so I began using my Verizon smart phone's fast charger on my lamp, and so far it seems to work better in less time. Not sure the factory would recommend that, but it seems to work all right.    If you haven't yet purchased one of these, I can also tell you that it is the best reading lamp I've EVER had, and I've tried many over the years. So, charge it up and read for weeks!

question_text: I have a soundboks 1 but it turns off when I put the volume at the highest.why?
answer_text: Hi there!     If you are playing directly with the charger and no battery it is perfectly normal that it shuts off at loud volume because the charger can provide a steady flow of power but not enough to keep the SOUNDBOKS going at full volume. However, the battery works as a readily available source of power that can provide a lot of power immediately to the SOUNDBOKS and keep it running at full volume.     The SOUNDBOKS 1 did however have a lower threshold than the SOUNDBOKS 2. Like in any other speakers, the units in the SOUNDBOKS can be damaged if you overload them too much. Since we wanted to create a user-friendly speaker that is unlikely to break no matter what, we decided to install a feature that shuts down the amplifier when the units are being heavily overloaded.     This means that if you connect the SOUNDBOKS to devices with high outputs, e.g., a mixer or certain smartphones, or play a highly compressed music file and crank up the volume to 100%, you could potentially experience the amplifier shutting down the speaker in order to protect itself. Usually taking the battery out and putting it back in again helps.    On a SOUNDBOKS 1, it is better to reduce the volume on the device that you're playing from and increase the volume from the SOUNDBOKS because the problem is caused by the high output levels from that device. We also recommend to play with less compressed music files, for example, with Spotify instead of Youtube.    For the SOUNDBOKS 2, we have modified this threshold so that the volume automatically readjusts itself when the speakers are overloaded rather than shutting down.     I hope this could answer your question. If you need help with your SOUNDBOKS 1, please feel free to reach out to us at info@soundboks.com and we'd be more than happy to help you.

answer_text: This happens with cheap tempered glass (btw, all tempered glass is cheap). Basically there are two types of glass that can handle heat: Borosilcate and tempered soda glass. Borosilcate expands and contracts with varying temperatures, so it rarely breaks and when it does it simply cracks. Tempered soda glass (which I'm ashamed to say makes up 99% of heat resistant glass here in the US) is basically glass that is strengthened to resist expansion and contraction Problem is, when it fails it literally explodes like a grenade. When it comes to cooking with glass, I only use borosilicate (its worth the price and the shipping costs to get it from Europe). I'm planning to buy this poacher, but I'll be using my own stainless steel lid and certainly not the soda glass cover.     I agree that it is a safety issue and feel that tempered soda glass should be illegal to manufacture and sell to consumers. This includes all tempered soda glass including that with which people do not cook because even cold drinking glasses made from tempered soda glass will, sooner or later, explode like grenades.

Once fitted to the wheel the two lock nuts sit on the valve cap side of the wheel rim. After fitment and inflation to the correct pressure, the two nuts should be backed up towards the valve cap, and locked against each other.    This is not usually an issue on correctly inflated road going tires, but should there be any slippage of tire on the rim, during heavy braking or acceleration for example, the inner tube could be pulled around slightly with the tire and if the inner tube is bolted to the rim the valve can be ripped out. If the lock nuts are raised towards the valve cap then inner tube has some leeway to move before this happens. Any movement is thus obvious as the valve stem will no longer be straight and pointing at the center of the hub, but will be pulled round at an angle.

question_text: This says it is shipped rolled up and to follow directions to unroll the mat.  What are the directions to unroll the mat?
answer_text: Hi,    Your mat has been rolled to allow economical and timely delivery. When vinyl mats are rolled they take on a “memory”” of that rolled shape and may be difficult to unroll when cold. The following precautions will protect your mat from cracking while enabling you to put it to use as soon as possible.Vinyl becomes more pliable with heat, so the warmer the mat the quicker it will lay flat. Also, the thicker the mat, the longer it will take for the mat to lay flat.    Always allow your mat to warm up thoroughly to (at least) room temperature before attempting to unroll your mat. (APPROX. 24 HOURS)    After the mat has warmed up, carefully unroll it and place it on the floor with the “bow” up (studs/cleats down), adding weight to hold the mat in place if necessary.The mat should gradually flatten over a period of a few hours ( thicker mats could take longer).         ADDITIONAL OPTIONS FOR UNROLLING YOUR MAT    Option #1    Try placing it in a small warm room (maybe a bathroom) or near a sunny window. Ideally once the temperature reaches approximately 80 degrees the mat will begin to relax quicker. At that point you can lay it flat bow side up. Add weight on top of the mat as needed.    Option #2 Warm Weather Method    Place your mat on a smooth flat surface outside in the sun on a warm sunny day until it flattens (check it every 15 minutes). After it relaxes and is flat move it to a flat cooler area (in the shade or indoors) until it cools and becomes more rigid. Now your mat is ready for installation. If you have any questions or need assistance please contact us.    Option #3 Cold Conditions and .220 or Thicker Mats    While the mat is still rolled in the box and standing on it’s end cut a hole in the middle of the top of the box. The hole should be big enough to allow the end of a portable hair dyer to be inserted. Place the end of the dryer that the warm air comes out of in the hole and turn the dryer on. Place the dryer so that the air will blow down the center of the rolled mat. Check the inside of the mat every 5 minutes to see if the mat is beginning to warm. The process of heating the interior core of the mat should take no longer than 15-20 minutes.    Once the core is warm take the mat out of the box and place the mat bow up on the floor. You will now need to heat the remainder of the mat. This can be done by slowly blowing warm air with hair dryer over the remainder of the mat. Starting with the warm area of the mat and working out toward the cool and rigid area of the mat. Move the hair dryer back and forth across sections of the mat until that sections warms and starts to relax. Repeat this process until the mat is completely relaxed. This process is recommended for thicker mats in cool climates. Putting weight on top of the mat can help speed the process. Please follow all manufacturer use and safety guidelines provided by hair dryer manufacturer.    Use extreme caution when using any of the suggested methods for relaxing your mats. They are only suggestions and we are not responsible for accidents or damage resulting from the use of any of these methods. You use them at your own risk.

Player with the highest population wins the turn, collects all the cards from that turn, puts them at the back of his deck and continues the turn.  Player on the turn always has an option of calling a CHALLENGE. In that case, he has to recognise an opponent's flag, name the capital city or show the opponents country on the map, depending which game mode they are playing. Depending on the thermostat you currently have, you may already have a wire in the C terminal. If you don't, some people have extra unused wires that can be found behind the wall. If you don't see them when you take your thermostat face-plate off the wall, they may be behind the sub-base. Typically, they will be part of the thermostat wire bundle. If you have an extra unused wire, you can connect it to the C terminal of the RTH6580 and then make sure that it is connected to the C terminal at your HVAC system. If you have a conventional furnace, you should have a furnace board that has terminals matching the terminals on the thermostat: R, W, Y, G, C. However, not every system is the same and if you have any questions during any part of this process, don't hesitate to give us a call at 1-855-733-5465 (ref case #01325899) and we will be happy to help you get everything figured out. -Kari

To save your adjustments, press and release the “gear/wrench” button to adjust the next preference.   The “wrench” icon will remain illuminated next to calibrated values.   The preference set order is as follows:   OUTDOOR TEMPERATURE   OUTDOOR HUMIDITY   INDOOR TEMPERATURE   INDOOR HUMIDITY   BAROMETRIC PRESSURE (must be set to MANUAL mode to calibrate)*   *To change from AUTO to MANUAL pressure mode and vice versa, press AND HOLD the “gear/wrench” button for at least 10 seconds.   The display indicates the current pressure mode selected, “AUTO” or “MANUAL”.   After 20 seconds of inactivity, the display will save the adjustments and exit calibration mode.   Note: Calibrations will be erased if the display is reset or if batteries are removed and the power adapter is unplugged. When the oil is added, add the pop corn and 1/2 teaspoon of  Flavocal [sold by Amazon]. The oil tastes buttery and like theater popcorn. Flavocal is the popcorn salt on theater popcorn [it is very fine grained].  Once the ingredients are in the pot I leave the tops resting on the retaining clips to allow steam to vent. I start stirring the pot as soon as I close the top. Take it off the heat when you think 98% is popped. Sometimes I melt butter and pour it on and shake, but that is a luxury. When you empty the popper make sure one of the tops is secured/closed with the  retaining clip.  IF you use it w/i 24 hours I just wipe it with a paper towel to get the excess oil off the insides.

question_text: Would the UV light in this device help to kill the flu virus?
answer_text: No!  UV lights on air purifiers are virtually useless and just a selling gimmick.  All bacteria, mold, yeast, and viruses are killed by UV light destroying their DNA.  For this to happen as quickly and efficiently as possible 3 things are needed.  #1 A light of the correct wavelength, for example 253.7 nanometers.  # 2 A light with the correct strength measured in µW/cm² .  #3 Time.  I looked in my manual and the first 2 are mentioned nowhere.  As for #3, the FLU virus needs about 8.25 seconds of UV light exposure at 800µW/cm² at a wavelength of 263.7 nanometers to be destroyed.  Even if the light in this unit met those parameters, there is no way that it will be exposed that long as the air flows by the lamp very quickly and isn't exposed for more than a fraction of a second.  Theoretically a virus could be killed, but it would have to pass thru the unit hundreds of times and the chances of that happening are virtually zero as once it passes through it will more than likely land on something.  I don't even use the light on mine.  It does a good job at removing dust though.

question_text: I waited until the propane grill was at 450 to 500 degrees, then put the matt on - hamburgers had no grill marks and were awful.  What did I do wrong?
answer_text: Hi Beth, thanks for your question. Hamburger,  especially high fat 80/20 burger, will release a lot of water while cooking. This water, if not removed, will cool the grill mats way down, to less than the boiling point of water which is 212 degrees around the burger.     This pooling water must be removed with tongs and paper towel,  pushing off with the back of a spatula, and/or moving the burger to a dry spot on the grill mat.    For best results in cooking burgers on a grill mat, we recommend low fat Hamburger. Many professional chefs who cook with high fat meats will sear off the meat at really high temperatures for a minute or so without the grill mat then transfer to the grill mat at a surface temperature of 350 degrees to finish. This ensures really tender juicy meat.    Long story short, grill mats are a tool that can be used in many different ways. Have fun experimenting and finding what works best.    The best temperature to grill at is 350 to 400 degrees at the grill surface. This is the temperature where most oils will begin to smoke. The lid thermometer will not show an approximation of the grill grate temperature unless you keep the lid closed for 20 minutes.

This allowed the angle of the sway bars to decrease (the pivot lifted up under load).   It happened several times on the road, and The back of the truck would suddenly dip down, and trailer jack sometimes scraped on driveways.  This also put all of the weight of the system on the mushroom head ‘stop’ between the hitch assy solid portion and pivoting portion and dug the mushroom head bolt into the solid hitch assy.      My fix was to adjust the system where I wanted it and weld the serrated washers permanently to the hitch assy.  The bolts can still be removed in case I wanted to remove the pivot assy for any reason.      I’m not sure if a more expensive load leveling hitch system would eliminate this issue or not, but if I were to do it again, I would spend more money on a more robust system if it is out there.  I’ve had this system for just under 2 years.
